items.followUp: What is a manometer used to measure?

rubric.why: Identifies what kind of thing a barometer is.
rubric.description: States that a barometer is an instrument or device.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as an instrument or device.

rubric.why: Checks that the measured quantity is correctly named.
rubric.description: States that a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Award for naming atmospheric pressure or air pressure.

modelAnswer: A barometer is an instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure.

items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the equation v_f² = v_i² + 2as.

rubric.why: Checks that the speed-time graph is correctly represented and labelled.
rubric.description: Shows time on the horizontal axis, speed on the vertical axis, and marks the points (0, vi) and (t, vf), joined by a straight line.
rubric.how: Award for the correctly labelled axes and initial and final speed points.

rubric.why: Checks the use of the area under the graph to express displacement.
rubric.description: Uses the area under the graph and writes S = vi t + 1/2 (vf − vi)t.
rubric.how: Award for identifying displacement with the area and writing the rectangle-plus-triangle expression.

rubric.why: Checks the acceleration relation needed for the substitution.
rubric.description: Uses a = (vf − vi)/t, or the equivalent vf − vi = at.
rubric.how: Award for the correct relation between acceleration, change in speed, and time.

rubric.why: Checks that the required second equation of motion is obtained.
rubric.description: Substitutes vf − vi = at into the area expression and obtains S = vi t + 1/2 at².
rubric.how: Award for the correct derived equation.

modelAnswer: Draw time on the horizontal axis and speed on the vertical axis.
Mark the initial-speed point (0, vi) and the final-speed point (t, vf), then join them with a straight line for uniform acceleration.
Displacement S is the area under the speed-time graph.
S = area of rectangle + area of triangle.

items.followUp: A 0.8 kg body moves in a circle of radius 0.4 m at 4 m s⁻¹. Calculate the centripetal force.

rubric.why: Checks that all given quantities are stated in SI units, including the radius conversion.
rubric.description: Lists m = 0.5 kg, r = 0.5 m and v = 3 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award for the correct mass, converted radius, and speed.

rubric.why: Checks selection of the centripetal-force formula.
Checks substitution of the SI data and correct evaluation.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the formula and evaluates the force as 9.
rubric.how: Award for correct substitution and arithmetic.

rubric.why: Checks the final force and its unit.
rubric.description: Gives the centripetal force as 9 N.
rubric.how: Award for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, r = 50 cm = 0.5 m, v = 3 m s⁻¹.
F_c = 4.5 kg m² s⁻² / 0.5 m = 9 kg m s⁻².
Therefore, the centripetal force required is 9 N.
